lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: the relationship between sine and cosine of complementary angles
lessonRef.title: Guided practice A: the relationship between sine and cosine of complementary angles

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Use this example as the model for the guided set below.

items.prompt: A 3-4-5 triangle, θ opposite the side 3. Find sin θ.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: A right triangle has hypotenuse 15 and one leg 9. Find the other leg.
Express sin 24° as a cosine of another angle, and explain why the two are equal.
choices: cos 66°, because the two angles are complementary and swap the roles of opposite and adjacent
cos 156°, because the angles are supplementary
cos 24°, because sine and cosine are always equal
cos 114°, because the angles differ by a right angle

items.prompt: From a point 12 m from the base of a tower, the angle of elevation to the top is θ, and the tower is 5 m tall. Which equation correctly determines θ?
choices: tan θ = 5/12
cos θ = 5/12
sin θ = 5/12
tan θ = 12/5

items.prompt: A right triangle has legs 3 and 4 and hypotenuse 5. Angle θ is opposite the leg of length 3. Find tan θ as an exact fraction in lowest terms.
A right triangle has legs 5 and 12. Find the hypotenuse.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Express sin 30° as a cosine of another angle, and explain why the two are equal.
choices: cos 120°, because the angles differ by a right angle
cos 150°, because the angles are supplementary
cos 30°, because sine and cosine are always equal
cos 60°, because the two angles are complementary and swap the roles of opposite and adjacent

items.prompt: From a point 8 m from the base of a tower, the angle of elevation to the top is θ, and the tower is 6 m tall. Which equation correctly determines θ?
choices: tan θ = 8/6
cos θ = 6/8
sin θ = 6/8
tan θ = 6/8

items.prompt: A right triangle has legs 24 and 45 and hypotenuse 51. Angle θ is opposite the leg of length 24. Find tan θ as an exact fraction in lowest terms.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

Express sin 53° as a cosine of another angle, and explain why the two are equal.
choices: cos 37°, because the two angles are complementary and swap the roles of opposite and adjacent
cos 127°, because the angles are supplementary
cos 53°, because sine and cosine are always equal
cos 143°, because the angles differ by a right angle
